name: two_sheets_and_the_same_projection_angle
why: ENTRY GT1. `export_pdf` already counts the pages of the PDF: it is the guard written because a PDF of a single sheet, on a drawing of three, comes out with no error and reaches the workshop incomplete. That count, however, was ALWAYS 1, because there was no way to make a second sheet. **A guard that can never fire is not a guard: it is a line of code that consoles.**
_the_projection_angle_is_the_whole_diffi: `NewSheet4` has `FirstAngle` as the sixth MANDATORY parameter: there is nothing to inherit, it must be decided at every sheet. Writing `false` because it is the default value would give the same drawing with two sheets mirrored differently -- neither of the two gives an error, and whoever cuts the part from sheet 2 cuts it upside down. The operation reads the projection angle of the current sheet, passes it on again, **and then re-reads it from the new sheet**: passing it is not having it.
_what_this_test_does_NOT_show: It does not prove that a sheet in third angle projection gets refused: here the drawing is born from the workshop template, which is first angle, and there is no way to ask for the third (it is not an argument of any operation, and it is deliberate). It proves that the TWO SHEETS AGREE, which is the thing that breaks through distraction.

expect.why: 120 x 80 x 10: the part the drawing is made on
a view attaches to the path of the part: it must be saved first
the bench follows the new document (entry GT0): without it, all the following steps would measure the part
**THE REFERENCE, and it comes first.** A drawing is born with one sheet. If this were not 1, «two afterwards» would not say that one was born.
the starting count, read by the operation itself
**THE SHEET IS COUNTED FROM `GetSheetNames().Length`, not from the Boolean that `NewSheet4` returns.** The value that comes back from whoever did the thing is not the measure of the thing.
a new sheet becomes the active one, and the operation re-reads it from `GetCurrentSheet` instead of taking it for granted

**THE THING THIS CASE EXISTS TO CATCH.** The drawing template of the workshop is in first angle projection; the new sheet must be in first angle too. This value is NOT the one passed to `NewSheet4`: it is the one **re-read from the new sheet** after the creation. If `NewSheet4` accepted the parameter and wrote another one, this expectation would turn red and no other would notice.
THE TWO READINGS AGREE: the operation says «created Montaggio», the state re-reads the drawing sheet by sheet and finds it in second place. Two independent roads.

and on the projection angle too. The state reads it from `GetProperties2()[4]` on its own, knowing nothing of what was passed to `NewSheet4`. **This is the second half of the comparison between the two sheets** -- the first arrives at the next step.
expect._why_only_for_this_sheet: The state writes `projection_angle` **only of the ACTIVE sheet**, and it is not an oversight: the properties of a sheet can be read only from the current one, and changing sheet to read them would be a reading that modifies. That is why the comparison between the two projection angles cannot be made in a single instant: this one is read now, and the first sheet at the next step, when it becomes active again.

expect.why: the new sheet is the active one, and the state says so as well as the operation

**THE ANSWER IS NOT TRUSTED.** The operation, after calling `ActivateSheet`, asks the drawing which sheet it has in front of it. If it were not the one asked for, the following steps would work on the wrong sheet -- and a view on the wrong sheet gives no error.
where we came from: without it, «active: Foglio1» would not say whether anything changed
the change really happened. Activating the sheet already active would succeed and do nothing, and it is a different case.
the second reading: the state marks «active» the sheet that the drawing declares current

**AND HERE THE COMPARISON CLOSES, which is the point of the whole case.** At the previous step, with the sheet «Assembly» active, the state said «first». Now, with «Foglio1» active, it says «first» too. **The two sheets agree** -- and it is the only thing that no other measure of this drawing would see: two sheets with different projection angles produce a plausible drawing, a complete PDF, and a part cut upside down. One sheet is read at a time because it is the only honest way: the properties are read from the active sheet, and changing sheet to read them would be a reading that modifies.
